questions.prompt: What makes machine learning different from a rule-based system?
options: It runs on faster computers
It learns patterns from examples instead of following rules a person wrote
It only works with images and voice
It never makes mistakes
questions.explanation: A rule-based system follows if-then rules that people write by hand. Machine learning studies lots of examples and works out the patterns itself, so it can handle cases nobody wrote a rule for.

questions.prompt: Your bank flags a ₹14,000 payment because it looks very different from your usual habits, judged against millions of past payments. What is doing the flagging?
options: A rule a developer wrote for that exact amount
Generative AI writing a warning message
A machine learning model trained on past payments
Nothing automatic: a bank employee checks every payment
questions.explanation: The system compares your payment with patterns it learned from millions of past payments. That's machine learning: nobody wrote a rule for this exact case, and it isn't creating anything new.

questions.prompt: Which order goes from the broadest idea to the narrowest?
options: Generative AI, deep learning, machine learning, AI
AI, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI
Machine learning, AI, generative AI, deep learning
Deep learning, AI, machine learning, generative AI
questions.explanation: AI is the broad goal. Machine learning is one way to reach it, deep learning is a kind of machine learning, and today's generative AI is built with deep learning. Each sits inside the one before it.

questions.prompt: You ask a chatbot to write a polite leave application for your manager, and it writes a fresh one in seconds. Which kind of AI is this?
options: Generative AI
A rule-based expert system
A search engine
Not AI at all
questions.explanation: The chatbot creates brand-new text instead of judging something that already exists. Creating new content is what makes it generative AI, and it runs on a large language model.

questions.prompt: What does "deep" mean in deep learning?
options: The model understands ideas deeply, like a person
The model was trained for a very long time
The neural network has many layers
The model stores the whole internet
questions.explanation: "Deep" just means the neural network has many layers, each one picking up a slightly more complex pattern than the one before. It says nothing about real understanding.

questions.prompt: A food app shows "Free delivery on orders above ₹199". Is that AI?
options: Yes, it's machine learning because the app uses data
Yes, it's generative AI because it shows a message
No, it's one fixed rule that a person wrote
Yes, it's deep learning because it runs on a phone
questions.explanation: It's a single if-then rule: if the total is above ₹199, delivery is free. Nothing is learned or predicted, so it's ordinary software, not AI.
